Algebra 2 | Quarter 2 | Unit 4: Quadratic Functions

Can the Rider Reach It?

What complex solutions really mean

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 10–11
Topic
Complex Solutions
Standards
HSN-CN.A.1, HSN-CN.A.2, HSN-CN.C.7

Students define i, add and multiply complex numbers, find complex solutions of quadratics with the quadratic formula, recognise conjugate pairs, and interpret complex roots as “never happens”.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Define i and write square roots of negative numbers in terms of i.
  • Add, subtract and multiply complex numbers.
  • Find complex solutions of quadratic equations and recognise conjugate pairs.
  • Explain what complex roots mean for a graph and in context.

3Essential question

If an equation has no real solution, what do its complex solutions tell us?

5MTB connection

Complex solutions have a real-world meaning: “this never happens.” A rider whose height equation gives complex times for 3 m simply never gets that high.

The real part of the complex pair is still useful: it is the time of the peak, the axis of symmetry of the height graph.

The mathOn the trail
Real solutionsTimes the rider passes a height
Complex solutionsThe rider never reaches that height
Double rootThe rider just touches it at the peak
Real partTime of the peak

7MTB activity

MTB Problem-Based Exercise

Can the Rider Reach It?

Use the quadratic formula to decide which heights a rider reaches, and interpret real and complex solutions.

You’ll need: Calculator; The height model h(t) = 1 + 6t − 4.9t2

The full lesson plan is for teachers

Teachers also get the mathematical foundation with worked examples, a 5-stage teaching plan with timings, step-by-step activity instructions, 4 guided examples with solutions, 9 practice problems, a 4-question exit ticket, a printable worksheet, common misconceptions, differentiation ideas and the complete answer key.
